newsitem.title: INDIA: Asian nations propose infrastructure action plan.
newsitem.headline: Asian nations propose infrastructure action plan.

text.p: A regional ministerial conference on infrastructure on Tuesday proposed an action plan to attract private investment and increase the pace of core projects in Asia and the Pacific.
The United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) released the "New Delhi Action Plan" on the second and last day of the ministerial conference.
Some 30 ESCAP member states were expected to approve the plan later on Tuesday, delegates said.
ESCAP estimates developing countries in the Asia-Pacific region need $1.5 trillion in new core sector development between 1993 and 2000, of which only $500 billion has been committed.
Investors in India, the conference's host country, complain that red tape and obscure guidelines have slowed investment in core sectors such as power, telecommunications and transport.
The plan proposes guidelines for increasing the efficiency of the infrastructure sector, raising confidence in the development process and creating an environment to attract private investment.
It says governments should streamline federal administrative controls and procedures, and ensure equitable sharing of risk between the private and public sectors.
"A clear picture of the government's long-term perception of the position of the private sector within its national strategy should be clearly elaborated," it says.
It also urges countries to make sure transport and trade documentation conforms with U.N. standards.
An environmental impact assessment should be made mandatory for all infrastructure projects, the plan says.
"The procedures and documentation for moving hazardous goods on transport infrastructure links and storing these goods at nodes should be reviewed and the necessary changes implemented," it says.
